situation: The maximum legal speed for cars should be lowered from 70mph to 60mph.
text: Overall, while I don't consider this an extremely pressing issue, I think this would be a good idea. It might reduce the number of accidents, but it would definitely help with noise pollution for people who live close to main roads. On the other hand, I suspect that a reduction of the speed limit may cause traffic to slow down. On the whole, I would argue that this should not be considered a top priority issue, and, if discussed in parliament, perhaps a solution where the limit is lowered under certain conditions but not others would be a good idea.

situation: The maximum legal speed for cars should be lowered from 70mph to 60mph.

It is likely the average person does need a car. For example, they may not live near easily accessible public transport and therefore need a car to get to work.

They may also have children they need to take places which isn’t really achievable without a car.

The average person is likely to drive late in the evening on occasions when it is usually not feasible or safe to use public transport.

At the same time, I can also understand why some parents might be hesitant to introduce these complex ideas at a young age, and might worry about how it will affect their child's own sense of identity and development. For me, I think the key is finding a way to approach the topic in a way that's both age-appropriate and sensitive to the needs and values of each individual family. I'm not sure what the right answer is, but I do think it's a conversation worth having.
